claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about your situation and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or do you have any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I do have a child. My son Alex is 8 years old, so he's under 16.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know you have Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now, to assess your eligibility, I need to understand your living situation:

**Do you currently live with Alex, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. He lives with his dad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex lives with his dad, I need to ask you about your financial contributions towards his care:

**Are you making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep, such as payments for food, clothes, pocket money, or other expenses? If so, could you tell me roughly how much you contribute and how often?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really able to contribute anything financially at the moment. I don't give anything towards his upkeep right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that. I have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the rules for Child Benefit when a child lives with someone else, you would normally qualify for 8 weeks after Alex went to live with his dad. However, since you're not making any financial contributions towards his upkeep, your entitlement would have ended after those 8 weeks.

Before I provide my final assessment, let me clarify one thing:

**How long ago did Alex go to live with his dad? Was it more or less than 8 weeks ago?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been quite a while now - several months ago actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex at the moment.

Here's why:

- While Alex is under 16 and would normally qualify, you are not considered responsible for him because he lives with his dad
- When a child lives with someone else, you can normally receive Child Benefit for 8 weeks after they move in
- Since Alex has been living with his dad for several months, this 8-week period has passed
- To continue receiving Child Benefit beyond those 8 weeks, you would need to contribute financially towards his upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.) at least equal to the Child Benefit payment amount
- You've indicated you're unable to make these contributions at the moment

**If your circumstances change in the future** – for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or if you're able to start making regular financial contributions towards his care – you could potentially become eligible again. If that happens, you should contact the Child Benefit Office to make a new claim.
